historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: FLAGGED: Equity CAGR is deeply negative (-6.13% over 3yr, -2.61% over 5yr) while Revenue CAGR is +10.52%/+13.06% and FCF CAGR is +10.03%/+13.17%. This is a share-buyback artifact, NOT business deterioration — Adobe has repurchased shares under $25B+ authorizations since FY2022, mechanically shrinking book value (FY2021 $14.8B to FY2025 $11.6B). Equity CAGR is excluded as the growth driver. FCF CAGR (3yr: 10.03%) is used as the primary driver, aligning with management FY2026 guidance of ~10% ARR/revenue growth.

base.description: Adobe sustains ~10% growth consistent with management FY2026 guidance, decelerating as AI competition incrementally weighs on Creative Cloud pricing power and subscriber growth slows at the margin. FCF margin held stable at ~41.5% (in line with FY2025). WACC of 10% reflects investment-grade balance sheet, estimated beta ~1.2, risk-free rate ~4.3%, and a moderate AI disruption risk premium.
base.growth_rationale: Y1 10% anchored to FY2026 guidance midpoint ($25.9-26.1B revenue). Y2 9% reflects continued Firefly/Acrobat AI Assistant momentum and Semrush contribution. Y3-Y4 deceleration as AI competition from Canva/OpenAI/Google incrementally pressures SMB/consumer tiers and creates pricing friction. Y5 5% reflects normalization toward terminal. Terminal 3% is consistent with long-run nominal GDP growth for a dominant SaaS platform.

bull.description: Firefly enterprise adoption accelerates meaningfully; AI book of business reaches $2B+ annualized run rate by FY2027. Acrobat AI Assistant captures significant share of the knowledge-worker PDF productivity market. GenStudio becomes a go-to enterprise content supply chain platform. Semrush proves accretive. FCF margin expands toward 44% via operating leverage. WACC of 9% reflects reduced execution risk as AI leadership becomes entrenched and discount rates ease.
bull.growth_rationale: Y1 15% reflects Semrush incremental contribution (~$200M) plus accelerating Firefly enterprise expansion on top of H1 FY2026 actual run rate (~12% YoY from Q1-Q2). Y2-Y3 sustained high-teens-then-double-digit growth as Business Professionals & Consumers segment (fastest growing at +15% in FY2025) scales. Y5 7% reflects durable creative/enterprise marketing moat. Terminal 3.5% reflects premium to GDP given secular digital content creation tailwind.

bear.description: Generative AI commoditizes creative tools faster than expected. Canva and Microsoft (bundled Copilot) force pricing concessions on Creative Cloud individual/SMB tiers; subscriber churn accelerates. Experience Cloud growth stalls below 5%. AI inferencing costs compress FCF margin toward 38%. WACC of 12% reflects elevated execution and structural disruption risk. Terminal growth 2%.
bear.growth_rationale: Y1 6% reflects guidance discounted significantly for AI competition risk and macro uncertainty. Y2-Y3 deceleration as Canva freemium and Microsoft bundling erode Creative Cloud's entry-level and SMB subscriber base. Y4-Y5 approaching terminal as structural headwinds from AI democratization of design dominate. Terminal 2% reflects risk that Adobe's long-run growth normalizes near GDP given intensifying AI-native competition.

sanity_check.diagnosis: PASS. Base IV of $444 implies 24.8x trailing P/E and 17.9x P/FCF — both BELOW Adobe's long-run historical median P/E of ~35x and below its typical FCF multiple range of 20-45x. The current market price ($206.43) implies only 11.5x trailing P/E and 8.3x P/FCF, which are multi-year lows for Adobe and suggest the market is pricing in significant and durable growth degradation. Even the bear case IV ($271.86) represents 31.7% upside from current price, and the bear case implies only ~14x trailing P/E at intrinsic value. The base DCF does NOT extrapolate peak earnings — it uses decelerating FCF growth (10% to 5%) and a conservative 10% WACC. The current price discount appears to reflect market fears around AI disruption and the stock's ~54% drawdown from its August 2024 peak of ~$574.
